groups.label: Find the Cartesian product of two finite sets

statements.text: If X and Y are two finite and non-empty sets, then $X\times Y=\{(a, b): a\in X, b\in Y\}$.
$X\times Y\neq Y\times X$ where $X\neq Y$.
The number of elements of X×Y equals that of Y×X, which equals the product of the numbers of elements of X and Y. Formula: $n(X\times Y)=n(Y\times X)=n(X)\times n(Y)$
n denotes the number of set elements.
If $(k, m)\in X\times Y$ then $k\in X$, $m\in Y$. Formula: $(k, m)\in X\times Y\Rightarrow k\in X, \ m\in Y$
If X is a non-empty set, then $X\times X=\{(a, b):a, b\in X\}$.
$X\times X$ is written $X^2$ and read 'X two'.

statements.text: If n(X) = 3, then n(X × X) = 3 × 3 = 9. Formula: $n(X)=3 \Rightarrow n(X\times X)=3\times 3=9$

groups.label: Represent N×N, Z×Z and Q×Q in the coordinate plane and identify points

statements.text: Step 1: Draw two perpendicular straight lines, one horizontal (xx') and the other vertical (yy'), intersecting at point O.
Step 2: Represent the natural numbers N on each of the horizontal and vertical lines, starting with the origin O which represents zero.
Step 3: Draw vertical and horizontal lines from the points representing the natural numbers; the points of intersection form the perpendicular graphical net of the cartesian product N × N.
Each point of this net represents one of the ordered pairs in the cartesian product N × N.
Represent the set of integers on each of the horizontal and vertical lines, where the point O represents the ordered pair (0, 0).
